answer: Jittered Arrival Windows.** Each identity's first packets must arrive inside a slot derived from a slowly refreshed secret, so agents cannot forge predictable join times. Traffic to a common wharf must show staggered, non-clustered inter-arrival spacing; bursts are dropped. An attacker pays by provisioning real-time randomness and dedicated egress per fake identity, since batching duplicates exposes correlated timing. Derived IDs resembling ivory tags are rotated, but each new identity still costs a fresh hardware clock skew and distinct network path.
